name: Close-Grip Bench Press
description: The close-grip bench press is a barbell pressing variation using a narrower grip (shoulder-width or slightly inside), which reduces pectoral involvement and shifts the primary load to the triceps. It allows heavy triceps training with more load than isolation exercises and is a staple accessory for pressing strength development.

execution.starting_position: Lie on a flat bench. Grip the barbell at shoulder width or slightly inside with an overhand grip. Unrack and hold with arms extended over the mid-chest.
execution.setup_instructions: Do not go excessively narrow — shoulder-width grip is sufficient. Going too narrow increases wrist stress without benefiting tricep isolation.
steps: Lower the bar to the lower chest keeping elbows tucked close to the torso.
Touch the chest and immediately press back to full arm extension.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale on descent, exhale on the press.
common_mistakes: Gripping too narrow — inside shoulder width increases wrist discomfort
Flaring the elbows wide, negating the tricep emphasis
safety_considerations: Use a spotter or rack safety catches
Keep thumbs wrapped around the bar
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension at top, bar touches lower chest at bottom.
coaching_cues: Keep elbows close to the body — tuck them in toward the ribs
Press the bar in a straight line upward
